description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its Private deployment offering (VPC + on‑prem/air‑gapped) to support enterprise-grade lifecycle management. This project, “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism,” implements a reliable, operator-friendly upgrade workflow across Private environments with strong prechecks, automatic backups, and deterministic rollback hooks.

Goals
- Provide a consistent, versioned upgrade workflow for Redwood Private (VPC and on‑prem) that is safe by default.
- Reduce upgrade-related incidents and support load by adding preflight validation (cluster health, storage capacity, version compatibility, RBAC/auth, networking) and clear failure modes.
- Enable rollback with defined hooks and data-plane/control-plane coordination (schema migrations, config/state, model cache handling).
- Produce auditable artifacts: upgrade plans, executed steps, backup/restore status, and a customer-facing changelog.

Scope
- Installer/orchestrator changes (redwood-private-installer) to support: staged upgrade plan generation, prechecks, backup/restore orchestration, and rollback entry points.
- Helm/Kubernetes packaging changes (redwood-helm-charts) for upgrade ordering, hooks, and safe rollouts.
- Terraform (redwood-terraform) updates for version pinning, artifact sources, and upgrade-related variables.
- Control-plane compatibility policies (in the main redwood repo) for version gating and “supported upgrade paths.”
- Operational docs/runbooks, change-management guardrails, and on-call procedures.

Non-goals (initial release)
- Full multi-hop automated upgrades across many major versions (will support N-1 → N as the default path initially).
- Automatic data migration for every historical schema edge case (will provide explicit “manual intervention required” guidance where needed).

Stakeholders and teams
- Product owner: Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments).
- Engineering: Ethan Park (Platform Control Plane), Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering), Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz (Infra), Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (SRE).
- Solutions/PS: Markus Klein, Bruno Silva, Fatima Noor (design partners, on-prem constraints).
- Security/Compliance: security review of rollback/backup handling and auditability.

Deliverables
- Design docs + ADRs covering upgrade phases, backup strategy, rollback semantics, and compatibility policy.
- Implementation across installer, charts, and platform gating + CI coverage.
- Runbooks and customer-facing operational guidance (internal + draft external snippets).
- Beta with 1–2 design partners (one VPC, one on-prem/air‑gapped), then GA.

Timeline (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): requirements gathering + design partner constraints; draft design + ADRs.
- Phase 1 (3–5 weeks): implement prechecks + upgrade plan + version gating; add CI/integration tests.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): backups + rollback hooks + docs/runbooks; beta rollout and hardening.
- Phase 3 (1–2 weeks): GA readiness (release notes, support playbooks, change management checklist).

files.description: Published overview of the end-to-end upgrade workflow for Private deployments: phases, invariants, required inputs, and operator UX (CLI/UI), including diagrams of control plane/data plane sequencing.
Detailed spec for preflight checks (Kubernetes health, storage headroom, DB connectivity, RBAC/SSO reachability, TLS/DNS, artifact availability), error messages, and remediation guidance.
Backup/restore design: what is backed up (db/config/secrets refs), encryption/KMS expectations, snapshot types (EBS, CSI, logical dumps), retention, and restore verification steps.
Defines rollback entry points, hook contracts, ordering rules, and how to handle partial upgrades, schema migrations, and model cache/state during rollback.
On-prem packaging doc for air-gapped upgrade bundles: artifact manifest, checksums/signing, offline dependency handling, and how the installer locates/verifies bundles.
Operator runbook: step-by-step procedure for performing upgrades, verifying success, handling common failures, and executing rollback safely.
ADR capturing the chosen upgrade-plan architecture (plan generation vs. imperative steps), rollback contract, and rejected alternatives (e.g., always-blue/green).
Change-management policy for Private releases: required prechecks, approval gates (SRE + Release Eng), communications templates, and risk scoring for customer environments.
CI plan for upgrade testing: supported Kubernetes versions, storage backends, VPC vs on-prem scenarios, and how nightly/PR gating tests are run.
SRE runbook for alerts triggered during upgrades (error rate spikes, DB migration issues, control-plane connectivity), including mitigation playbooks and escalation rules.
PR adding an upgrade plan generator to the private installer: produces a staged plan, validates required artifacts, and outputs an auditable plan summary.
PR introducing a pluggable preflight check framework with standardized results, severity levels, and remediation pointers.
PR adding backup orchestration (snapshot hooks + logical backup option), including progress reporting and failure handling.
PR implementing rollback command that consumes stored upgrade state, executes rollback hooks, and verifies post-rollback health.
PR adding checksum/signature verification for offline bundles and clearer messaging for missing/incorrect artifacts.
PR updating Helm hooks and job ordering for safe upgrades, including timeouts and rollback-safe behaviors.
PR separating chart phases to ensure control plane upgrades complete before data plane changes; includes readiness gates.
PR adding Terraform variables for version pinning, upgrade windows, and artifact source configuration for Private deployments.
PR enabling artifact mirror endpoints and offline registries for on-prem customers, with validation and docs updates.
PR adding a version compatibility matrix/policy evaluation used to block unsupported upgrade paths and warn on risky jumps.
PR emitting audit log events for upgrade lifecycle (start, prechecks pass/fail, backup complete, rollback invoked) for enterprise traceability.
PR adding DB migration guardrails (idempotency checks, lock timeouts, safe defaults) to reduce upgrade-induced outages.
PR updating internal/external-ish docs pages: upgrade steps, troubleshooting, and rollback guidance aligned to new installer commands.
PR improving incident-bot tagging/annotation so incidents triggered during upgrade windows are labeled and linked to release artifacts.
PR adding dashboards for upgrade health: precheck failure rates, migration durations, error rates during upgrade windows, and rollback frequency.
